newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Crew feared dead as cargo ship sinks off S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Crew feared dead as cargo ship sinks off S.Africa.

text.p: A Panamanian registered cargo ship sank off South Africa's Indian Ocean coast and all 29 crew were feared dead, port officials said on Thursday.
"There are 29 crewmen who we assume have been killed in the incident," port of Durban captain Ron Holloway told Reuters.

He said the 12,000 tonne mixed-cargo ship named Cordigliera, had set off from the port of Durban at about 10:30 GMT on Wednesday, en route to Cape Town and the west African cities of Abidjan and Lagos.

It later radioed in a distress call at about 00:30 GMT, on Thursday shortly before going aground when it began taking in water, about five nautical miles east of Port St Johns on South Africa's Wild Coast, Holloway said.
"We have found no survivors and our search and rescue teams with the assistance of helicopters are busy combing the area," he said.
Patches of debris including three-badly damaged life rafts, paper reels and a stretch of oil had been found in the vicinity.
